summary: Snapshot-driven traffic snapback: safe revert guidance after aggressive optimizer profile introduced tail 5xx and session timeouts
description: Issue summary: FinSight enabled an aggressive optimizer profile (async micro-batching + aggressive per-token quantization + KV prefetch) on their Dedicated pool. Within 10 minutes, they reported elevated tail latency, an increase in 502/504 responses for long-stream sessions, and client-observed session timeouts. Impact: Several key analytics pipelines degraded (approx 18% error rate for streaming requests), user-facing dashboards reported stale data, and retries increased cost. Environment: Dedicated GPU pool (prod-us-east), pinned model: gpt-open-7b-v2-quant, traffic split: 100% after config push. Initial action requested: stepwise, low-risk revert procedure that preserves in-flight sessions and avoids a global cold-start that would further spike latency.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On a dedicated pool with model gpt-open-7b-v2-quant, apply optimizer profile: async_micro_batch=true, kv_prefetch=enabled, quant_profile=aggressive_4bit
2) Route steady streaming traffic from FinSight tenant (session affinity ON) at 150rps to the pool
3) Observe key metrics within 5-15 minutes: 95p/99p latency increase, increasing 5xx rate for streaming endpoints, and client session disconnects
comments: Aisha Patel (Support): Customer reports increase in streaming 5xx and session disconnects after optimizer change; asked for urgent safe rollback plan.
Miguel Ortega (SRE): Confirmed spike on prod-us-east. Hypothesis: aggressive KV prefetch + quant-induced eviction causing repeated cold KVs and retry storms. Will prioritize snapshot approach.
FinSight (Customer): Need to avoid full restart — long-lived streaming sessions are critical. Can we do staged revert with minimal interruption?
Miguel Ortega (SRE): Drafting stepwise plan (below). Will coordinate a 30-minute maintenance window if required.
investigation_notes: Telemetry shows KV cache churn on shards hosting large session state — eviction rate increased x6 after kv_prefetch toggled.
Quantization path increased per-token CPU on host side in the fallback path, amplifying queueing under CPU saturation.
Serving runtime logs indicate repeated model reload attempts for some shards during heavy async batching bursts — correlated with 502s.
proposed_action_plan: 1) Take a per-tenant snapshot of optimizer configuration and runtime state (use /admin/snapshot?tenant=finSight). Store snapshot with timestamped tag.
2) Enable a soft-circuit on routing: create a 10% diversion to a warmed fallback variant (gpt-open-7b-v2-std) to validate traffic path without touching all sessions.
3) For remaining 90% traffic, initiate a staged snapback: toggle kv_prefetch=disabled on 25% of dedicated nodes at a time and observe 5-minute steady-state before moving to next cohort.
4) If a cohort shows reduced 5xx and tail latency improvement, expand snapback to 50% then 100%. Keep metrics gating at each step (95p latency, 5xx rate, request_queue length).

5) If streaming clients require session preservation: enable session-forwarding pin for affected sessions to nodes in cohorts being snapbacked; ensure session tokens are copied to fallback nodes before revocation.
6) Once kv_prefetch is fully disabled and system steady, roll quant_profile from aggressive_4bit -> conservative_8bit in a 2-stage rollout (canary 10% then 100%).
7) Rehydrate KV caches proactively on cohorts after toggles using low-rate synthetic warmup traffic to rebuild hot prefixes (use the warmup tool: /tools/warmup-sessions).
8) After full revert, run a 30-minute soak with close monitoring; keep rollback snapshot available for immediate restore if degradation recurs.
9) Post-action: collect traces and a diff of model latencies pre/post, and schedule a postmortem with FinSight to decide safer optimizer guardrails.
mitigation_attempts: Customer rolled back traffic split to 50/50 between tuned and fallback manually which reduced errors by ~40% but did not fully resolve tail latency.
Support disabled async_micro_batch flag on 2 nodes as a quick experiment which temporarily reduced queue length but revealed KV eviction still high.
Applied temporary request-level retry limiter at the gateway to avoid retry amplification.
resolution_notes: PENDING - executing staged snapshot-driven snapback per plan. Will update when 100% snapback completed and metrics stabilized. Follow-up: create conservative optimizer gating policy for FinSight to prevent auto-enabling aggressive profiles without staged rollout and canary metrics.
postmortem_followups: 1) Add optimizer experiment runbook for Dedicated customers that includes mandatory snapshot and canary traffic split steps.
2) Implement automatic detection for KV-churn anomalies tied to optimizer toggles and trigger automated rollback gate.
3) Create a tenant-level 'safe-enable' flag that requires a warmup and KV-rehydration step before full traffic switch.
4) Document warmup best practices in customer onboarding docs and provide FinSight a tailored warmup script.
